open_obligations: Note that Theorem 5.1 covers time-T, space-S oracle computations, while Irving et al.'s Theorem 1 covers all of PSPACE.
Check that the oracle model of human judgement corresponds to Irving et al.'s polynomial-time judge H.
Check what each entry of the (O(T log T), O(S log T), O(1)) triple measures, and the role of O(S log T) when S is large.
Check whether Brown-Cohen et al. build on Irving et al.'s debate and whether their honest prover is efficient while the dishonest prover is unbounded; the cited passages state neither.
out.other_title: Theorem 1: debate with a polynomial-time judge and optimal play decides PSPACE
out.rationale: Irving et al.'s Theorem 1 shows polynomial-step debate with a polynomial-time judge decides PSPACE under optimal play. Brown-Cohen et al.'s Theorem 5.1 gives a bisection protocol (A states a middle configuration, B picks a half) deciding any time-T, space-S oracle computation as an (O(T log T), O(S log T), O(1))-debate protocol, which the authors compare with doubly-efficient interactive proofs.
out.scope: proposed SAME_QUESTION_DIFFERENT_SETTING: which computations a debate can decide, for PSPACE problems with a polynomial-time judge under optimal play versus time-T, space-S oracle Turing machine computations

text: Theorem 5.1 states that any language decidable by an oracle Turing machine M in time T and space S has an (O(T log T), O(S log T), O(1))-debate protocol that deterministically decides it. In the protocol A outputs a supposed middle configuration of the computation of M(x) and B decides which half to recurse on, bottoming out at a single transition of the machine M. The authors compare this with single-prover doubly-efficient interactive proofs, where Reingold et al. [2021] decide any time-T space-S computation in time O(S^2 polylog T) (whether this can be improved to O(S polylog T) is open) with a complex protocol that relies on prior work including the PCP theorem and so does not apply in the presence of a black-box oracle.
title: Theorem 5.1: (O(T log T), O(S log T), O(1))-debate protocol for time-T, space-S computations
